intro: Amazon's Q3 numbers landed, and Reddit and Google are openly at odds over whether AI search sends any traffic.

must_reads.title: Amazon’s Ads nears $20 billion in Q3 as it bets on agentic AI to fuel further growth
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Amazon's retail and ad business is leaning harder into AI agents that shop for people. If agents do more of the buying, fewer clicks go through creators' links, so how links get credit becomes a bigger question for everyone in affiliate.

must_reads.title: Reddit’s CEO says Google’s AI Mode ‘does not drive traffic’
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: A big publisher saying Google's AI answers don't send visitors is a clear sign that search traffic to content is shrinking. Creators and publishers who rely on Google will lean more on their own audiences and social links, which is where smart links live.

must_reads.title: Here’s Why You’re About to See More Ads in Google’s AI Overviews
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Google is putting more paid placements inside AI answers. Paid ads pushing organic results further down makes it harder for affiliate content to get seen in search.

must_reads.title: DoorDash Acquires Instacart As Consolidation Comes For Mobility Media
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Big shopping and delivery apps are merging, so fewer, bigger stores control where buyers end up. Creators and brands linking to products need tools that work across whichever stores win.

must_reads.title: My Amazon Affiliate links may be getting hit by bot clicks.
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Real creators are worried about bot clicks on their Amazon links. Click quality and bot filtering are a live concern for link users, not just a technical detail.
